patches.value: Let a and b denote the abstract raising and lowering Chevalley generators, namely the first and second standard matrices in L_Z, included in sl2(C) and then its universal enveloping algebra. U_Z is the integer subalgebra of that enveloping algebra generated by {a^r/r!, b^r/r! : integers r>=0}. In the given representation these elements act as X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! on V. The represented endomorphisms x,y need not give a faithful representation.

value.type: abstract raising Chevalley generator in L_Z and its canonical image in the enveloping algebra
abstract lowering Chevalley generator in L_Z and its canonical image in the enveloping algebra

patches.value: Fix an arbitrary rational q0 and assume L1: q0!=0. Its signed integer numerator has nonzero absolute value, and its denominator is a positive natural number. Apply M005 to each of these two nonzero natural numbers, setting its q-parameter to p; H001 gives p>=2, hence p!=1. Choose the resulting pairs (alpha0,A0) and (beta0,B0), so abs(num(q0))=p^alpha0 A0, den(q0)=p^beta0 B0, and neither A0 nor B0 is divisible by p. Both remainders are nonzero, since the numerator and denominator are nonzero. Define d0=alpha0-beta0 and let u0 be A0/B0 with the sign of num(q0). Then q0=p^d0 u0. Both u0 and its inverse have denominator not divisible by p, so u0 is a unit of R. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q0. This proves the scalar decomposition for every nonzero rational, allowing either sign of the integer exponent.

value.declaration: Fix an arbitrary rational q0; its nonzeroness is assumed only within L1.
Choose the exponent alpha0 in a pair (alpha0,A0) supplied by M005 for the nonzero absolute numerator of q0.
Choose the remainder A0 in that same M005 pair: abs(num(q0))=p^alpha0 A0 and p does not divide A0.
Choose the exponent beta0 in a pair (beta0,B0) supplied by M005 for the positive denominator of q0.
Choose the remainder B0 in that same M005 pair: den(q0)=p^beta0 B0 and p does not divide B0.
Define u0=A0/B0 if num(q0)>0 and u0=-A0/B0 if num(q0)<0. The nonzero denominator and the sign dichotomy are established in S004 before this definition is used.

patches.value: For the arbitrary nonzero rational q0 use a=abs(num(q0)) and then a=den(q0); set the source parameter q=p in both applications. Choose the respective pairs (alpha0,A0) and (beta0,B0).
